questions.question: An owner reports that the rear wheel wells of their vehicle were found rusted. Which recall campaigns for that vehicle did NHTSA receive in 2015?

chunks.quote: IT WAS DISCOVERED THAT THE REAR WHEEL WELLS WERE RUSTED.

questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT r.NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r JOIN complaints c ON c.product.productModel = r.Model WHERE c.odiNumber = 10667633 AND r.ReportReceivedDate LIKE '%/2015'
questions.note: The complaint is 10667633 about the 2015 Ford Escape. Of its nine recalls, 15V406000 (24/06/2015) and 15V436000 (08/07/2015) were received in 2015; recall dates are day/month/year.

questions.question: An owner reports that the exterior rearview mirrors of their vehicle shook and rattled. How many recall campaigns affect that vehicle?

chunks.quote: THE EXTERIOR REARVIEW MIRRORS SHOOK AND RATTLED.

questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT count(*) FROM r JOIN complaints c ON c.product.productModel = r.Model WHERE c.odiNumber = 11205702
questions.note: The complaint is 11205702 about the 2019 Toyota RAV4, which has seven recall campaigns in the data: 20V682000, 20V064000, 20V373000, 20V286000, 19V503000, 19V576000 and 19V244000.

questions.question: An owner reports that the speedometer of their vehicle failed without warning. Which recall campaigns for that vehicle did NHTSA receive in 2017 or earlier?

chunks.quote: THE CONTACT STATED THAT THE SPEEDOMETER FAILED WITHOUT WARNING.

questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT r.NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r JOIN complaints c ON c.product.productModel = r.Model WHERE c.odiNumber = 10957753 AND CAST(right(r.ReportReceivedDate, 4) AS INTEGER) <= 2017
questions.note: The complaint is 10957753 about the 2017 Nissan Rogue. 16V244000 (26/04/2016) and 17V663000 (18/10/2017) qualify; 21V839000 (2021), 22V875000 (2022) and 23V093000 (2023) do not. The cut at 2017 keeps out 21V839000, whose summary speaks only of Rogue Hybrid vehicles.

questions.question: An owner reports that, with adaptive cruise control and lane keeping assist engaged together, their car reacts unpredictably. Which recall campaigns for that car did NHTSA receive after 2020?

chunks.quote: THE VEHICLE WILL REACT UNPREDICTABLY UNDER CERTAIN CONDITIONS.

questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT r.NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r JOIN complaints c ON c.product.productModel = r.Model WHERE c.odiNumber = 10816192 AND CAST(right(r.ReportReceivedDate, 4) AS INTEGER) > 2020
questions.note: The complaint is 10816192 about the 2016 Honda Civic. 23V858000 was received 18/12/2023 and 26V332000 on 21/05/2026; the other three Civic recalls are from 2016.

questions.question: A recall campaign warns that water may leak into and corrode the dash side harness connector. Which components do the owner complaints about that vehicle list?

chunks.quote: Water may leak into and corrode the dash side harness connector.

questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT DISTINCT trim(x) FROM (SELECT unnest(string_split(c.components, ',')) AS x FROM complaints c JOIN r ON r.Model = c.product.productModel WHERE r.NHTSACampaignNumber = '22V875000')
questions.note: The recall is 22V875000 for the 2017 Nissan Rogue. Its five complaints list ELECTRICAL SYSTEM (10957753), FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE (10972343), SERVICE BRAKES (11010220), POWER TRAIN (11030208) and FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM (11032133).

questions.question: Which complaints about the vehicle affected by recall 19V493000 list visibility/wiper among their components?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT c.odiNumber FROM complaints c JOIN r ON r.Model = c.product.productModel WHERE r.NHTSACampaignNumber = '19V493000' AND c.components LIKE '%VISIBILITY/WIPER%'
questions.note: 19V493000 affects the 2019 Subaru Outback. 11180230 lists VISIBILITY/WIPER alone and 11166434 lists it with ELECTRICAL SYSTEM and VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL. The RAV4 complaint 11205702 lists VISIBILITY (no wiper) and is about another vehicle.

questions.question: An owner reports that they can smell freon in their vehicle. Which recall campaign for that vehicle concerns its suspension?

chunks.quote: ALSO YOU CAN SMELL FREON.

questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT r.NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r JOIN complaints c ON c.product.productModel = r.Model WHERE c.odiNumber = 11229137 AND r.Component LIKE 'SUSPENSION%'
questions.note: The complaint is 11229137 about the 2019 Toyota RAV4. Its only suspension recall is 20V286000 (component SUSPENSION:FRONT:CONTROL ARM:LOWER ARM, cracked front lower suspension arms).

questions.question: Which complaints concern a vehicle that has a steering recall campaign?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT c.odiNumber FROM complaints c JOIN r ON r.Model = c.product.productModel WHERE r.Component LIKE 'STEERING%'
questions.note: The only recall whose component is steering is 20V373000 (STEERING:ELECTRIC POWER ASSIST SYSTEM), for the 2019 Toyota RAV4; its five complaints are the answer. Complaints that list STEERING themselves (10816192, 11176393) do not count: the question asks about the vehicle's recalls.

questions.question: An owner says that at highway speeds their car feels like driving on ice. What will dealers do under that vehicle's recall for its body structure?

expected.text: Inspect the vehicles and repair or repurchase the vehicle, as necessary, free of charge.

chunks.quote: IT FEELS LIKE DRIVING ON ICE.
dealers will inspect the vehicles and repair or repurchase the vehicle, as necessary, free of charge.

questions.note: The complaint is 11176393 about the 2019 Subaru Outback; its structure recall is 19V493000 (improperly applied spot welds below the cowl panel).

questions.question: How many complaints list the engine among their components?
questions.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM complaints WHERE components LIKE '%ENGINE%'
questions.note: 10823637, 10824361 and 10825467 (2016 Honda Civic) list ENGINE, and 11209676 (2019 Toyota RAV4) lists POWER TRAIN,ENGINE,FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM.

questions.question: How many different companies are named as the filer (the Manufacturer field) of the recall campaigns?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT count(DISTINCT Manufacturer) FROM r
questions.note: Honda (American Honda Motor Co.); Nissan North America, Inc.; Toyota Motor Engineering & Manufacturing; Southeast Toyota Distributors, LLC; Gulf States Toyota, Inc.; Ford Motor Company; Subaru of America, Inc. The two distributors are named as filers in their own right, so the three Toyota names count separately.

questions.question: How many recall campaigns did NHTSA receive in 2022?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT count(*) FROM r WHERE ReportReceivedDate LIKE '%/2022'

questions.question: Which complaints report an incident on the same date as another complaint's incident?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints WHERE dateOfIncident IN (SELECT dateOfIncident FROM complaints GROUP BY dateOfIncident HAVING count(*) > 1)
questions.note: 10823637 and 10824361 (2016 Honda Civic) both give 01/30/2016; 11185059 (2019 Subaru Outback) and 11229137 (2019 Toyota RAV4) both give 03/01/2019. 10667633 (12/20/2014) and 11209676 (12/20/2018) share only day and month.

questions.question: How many recall campaigns list a component under ELECTRICAL SYSTEM?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT count(*) FROM r WHERE Component LIKE 'ELECTRICAL SYSTEM%'
questions.note: 22V875000 (ELECTRICAL SYSTEM:WIRING), 23V093000 (ELECTRICAL SYSTEM:IGNITION:...), 15V406000 (ELECTRICAL SYSTEM: INSTRUMENT CLUSTER/PANEL) and 15V436000 (ELECTRICAL SYSTEM:IGNITION). 26V011000 (EQUIPMENT:ELECTRICAL:ENGINE BLOCK HEATER) is under EQUIPMENT and does not count.

questions.question: Counting each comma-separated component of a complaint separately, how many distinct components appear across all complaints?
questions.sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT trim(x)) FROM (SELECT unnest(string_split(components, ',')) AS x FROM complaints)
questions.note: UNKNOWN OR OTHER, STEERING, VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL, ENGINE, ELECTRICAL SYSTEM, FORWARD COLLISION AVOIDANCE, SERVICE BRAKES, POWER TRAIN, FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM, VISIBILITY, STRUCTURE, AIR BAGS, VISIBILITY/WIPER. VISIBILITY and VISIBILITY/WIPER are different values.

questions.question: Which recall campaign did NHTSA receive most recently?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r ORDER BY strptime(ReportReceivedDate, '%d/%m/%Y') DESC LIMIT 1
questions.note: 26V332000 was received 21/05/2026, after 26V011000 (15/01/2026); recall dates are day/month/year.

questions.question: Which recall campaign did NHTSA receive earliest?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r ORDER BY strptime(ReportReceivedDate, '%d/%m/%Y') ASC LIMIT 1
questions.note: 15V406000 was received 24/06/2015, before 15V436000 (08/07/2015); recall dates are day/month/year.

questions.question: Which complaints say that the dealer could not duplicate the failure, using the word 'duplicate'?

chunks.quote: THE VEHICLE WAS TAKEN TO HALL NISSAN IN CHESAPEAKE, VA, BUT THE FAILURE COULD NOT BE DUPLICATED.
THE TOYOTA DEALER COULD NOT DUPLICATE THIS AT THE 5000 MILE INSPECTION

questions.note: 11030208 (2017 Nissan Rogue) and 11209676 (2019 Toyota RAV4). Not counted: 10690483, whose first visit found 'NO PROBLEM FOUND' before a later visit diagnosed the left rear brake, and 11176393, where the dealer said nothing is wrong; neither uses the word.

questions.question: Which complaints list more than one component?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints WHERE components LIKE '%,%'
questions.note: Components are comma-separated in the complaint records: 10692693 (POWER TRAIN,FUEL/PROPULSION SYSTEM), 10816192 (STEERING,VEHICLE SPEED CONTROL), 11166434 (three components), 11209676 (three components).

questions.question: Which recall campaigns list seats or seat belts as their component?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r WHERE Component LIKE 'SEAT%'
questions.note: 17V663000 (SEATS, 2017 Nissan Rogue) and 17V472000 (SEAT BELTS, 2015 Ford Escape). 16V244000 and 26V332000 concern passenger seat sensors but their component is AIR BAGS.

questions.question: Which complaints report an incident that happened in 2018?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints WHERE dateOfIncident LIKE '%/2018'
questions.note: By the incident date, not the filing date: 11123359 (incident 08/28/2018) and 11209676 (incident 12/20/2018, filed 05/24/2019).

questions.question: Which complaints about the 2015 Ford Escape were filed in March 2015?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints WHERE product.productModel = 'ESCAPE' AND dateComplaintFiled LIKE '03/%/2015'
questions.note: Complaint dates are month/day/year: 10691672 was filed 03/02/2015 and 10692693 on 03/07/2015.

questions.question: Which recall campaigns list a component under ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r WHERE Component LIKE 'ENGINE AND ENGINE COOLING%'
questions.note: 16V074000 (2016 Honda Civic), 20V064000 (2019 Toyota RAV4) and 21V839000 (2017 Nissan Rogue, ...:ENGINE CONTROL MODULE). 26V011000's engine block heater is under EQUIPMENT.

questions.question: Which complaints were filed in a calendar year earlier than the model year of the vehicle they concern?
questions.sql: SELECT c.odiNumber FROM complaints c JOIN vehicles v ON v.model = c.product.productModel WHERE CAST(right(c.dateComplaintFiled, 4) AS INTEGER) < v.model_year
questions.note: 10667633 (filed 2014, 2015 Ford Escape), 10809523 and 10816192 (filed 2015, 2016 Honda Civic), 11123359 (filed 2018, 2019 Subaru Outback).

questions.question: Which complaints about the 2017 Nissan Rogue were filed more than 7 days after the incident?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints WHERE product.productModel = 'ROGUE' AND date_diff('day', strptime(dateOfIncident, '%m/%d/%Y'), strptime(dateComplaintFiled, '%m/%d/%Y')) > 7
questions.note: 10957753: incident 02/05/2017, filed 03/01/2017 (24 days). 10972343 was filed exactly 7 days after (04/06 to 04/13/2017), which is not more than 7; the others within 6 days.

questions.question: Which complaints were filed in February of any year?
questions.sql: SELECT odiNumber FROM complaints WHERE dateComplaintFiled LIKE '02/%'
questions.note: Complaint dates are month/day/year: two in February 2015 (Ford Escape), three in February 2016 (Honda Civic), two in February 2019 (Subaru Outback).

questions.question: Which recall campaigns affecting the 2017 Nissan Rogue or the 2015 Ford Escape did NHTSA receive in 2016?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSACampaignNumber FROM r WHERE Model IN ('ROGUE', 'ESCAPE') AND ReportReceivedDate LIKE '%/2016'
questions.note: 16V244000 (Rogue, 26/04/2016) and 16V643000 (Escape, 06/09/2016); recall dates are day/month/year.

questions.question: Two fuel pump recall campaigns in the data say they are expansions of earlier recalls. Which one expands recall 20V-012?

chunks.quote: Note: This recall is an expansion of recall 20V-012.

questions.note: 20V682000 (Toyota, 2019 Toyota RAV4). The other expansion, 23V858000 (Honda, 2016 Honda Civic), expands NHTSA recall numbers 21V-215 and 20V-314. The Subaru fuel pump recalls name no earlier recall.

questions.question: Of the two Ford door latch recalls, which one began on January 27, 2017?

chunks.quote: The recall began on January 27, 2017.

questions.note: The other door latch recall, 20V331000, re-inspects earlier repairs; its owner letters were mailed July 27, 2020. The pair 16V643000/20V331000 was used before (H24), with a different distinguishing detail.

questions.question: Two recall campaigns concern the ignition system. Which one warns that the engine may continue to run after the key or the START/STOP button is turned off?

chunks.quote: the engine may continue to run after the key or the START/STOP engine button is turned to off.

questions.note: 15V436000 (2015 Ford Escape, component ELECTRICAL SYSTEM:IGNITION). The other ignition recall, 23V093000 (2017 Nissan Rogue), is about a jackknife key that may collapse and shut the vehicle off.

questions.question: Of the two load label recalls affecting the 2019 Toyota RAV4, which one is limited to vehicles equipped with factory-installed floor mats?

chunks.quote: Yaris iA vehicles equipped with factory-installed floor mats.

questions.note: 19V244000 (Gulf States Toyota) concerns load capacity label text that may become illegible and has no floor mat condition. The pair 19V244000/19V503000 was used before (H26), with a different distinguishing detail.

questions.question: Of the two recall campaigns about a back-up or rearview camera, which one is run as a phased campaign?

chunks.quote: This will be a phased campaign, with the remedy becoming available in different phases based on model and model years.

questions.note: The camera recalls are 19V576000 (2019 Toyota RAV4) and 25V695000 (2015 Ford Escape); only the Ford one is phased.

questions.question: Two 2016 Honda Civic owners complain about a piston ring recall. Which complaint says Honda customer service told them there would be no fix until mid-March?

chunks.quote: PISTON CLIP RING RECALL FROM HONDA WITH NO FIX UNTIL MID-MARCH AS TOLD BY HONDA CUSTOMER SERVICE.

questions.note: 10825467 (piston snap ring recall) says only that Honda currently has no fix, with no date.

questions.question: Two 2019 Subaru Outback owners report a cracked windshield. Which complaint says the windshield cracked while driving on the highway?

chunks.quote: UNDER THE WIPER BLADE WHILE DRIVING ON THE HIGHWAY.

questions.note: In 11123359 the crack appeared overnight on the 4th day of ownership.

questions.question: Two 2019 Subaru Outback owners report a dead battery. Which complaint blames the drain on the navigation system staying on at night?

chunks.quote: SYSTEMS STAYS ON AT NIGHT DRAINING BATTERY.

questions.note: 11185059 describes a parasitic drain with nothing left on and names no cause.

questions.question: Which complaints report that a repair fixed the problem?

chunks.quote: NO CHANGE. SQUEAL RETURNED IN TWO DAYS.
THE VEHICLE IS AGAIN STALLING AT TRAFFIC LIGHTS UPON ACCELERATION.

questions.note: The two complaints with repair work say the problem came back: 10690483 (pads changed, rotors machined, squeal returned) and 10692693 (transmission parts replaced, stalling again). 10689793 says no repairs were needed or made; the others were not repaired or only await a repair.

questions.question: Which vehicles do owners report with a check engine light coming on?

chunks.quote: THERE ARE NO CODES SET NOR DOES IT SET A CHECK ENGINE LIGHT WHEN IT HAPPENS.

questions.note: The only mention of a check engine light (11209676, 2019 Toyota RAV4) says the light does not come on, so no vehicle qualifies.

questions.question: In complaint 10689793, did the Ford dealer and manufacturer deny that the accelerator hesitation was occurring?

expected.text: No. They explained the hesitation but did not deny that it was occurring.

chunks.quote: FORD DEALER AND FORD MANUFACTURER EXPLAIN HESITATION BUT DO NOT DENY IT IS OCCURRING.

questions.question: In complaint 11185059, could the dead battery be revived with a jump start?

expected.text: No. The battery would not take a jump and had to be fully recharged each time.

chunks.quote: NEEDING TO BE FULLY RECHARGED AS IT WOULDN'T TAKE A JUMP.

questions.question: Which complaints say a rock chip caused their cracked windshield?

chunks.quote: I WAS NOT FOLLOWING ANY VEHICLES SO A ROCK CHIP COULD NOT BE THE CAUSE.
NO VISIBLE CHIP DAMAGE APPARENT.

questions.note: Both windshield complaints rule a chip out: 11180230 says a rock chip could not be the cause and 11123359 says no chip damage is visible.

questions.question: Which complaints about the 2019 Toyota RAV4 say that the manufacturer was notified of the failure?

chunks.quote: THE MANUFACTURER WAS MADE AWARE OF THE FAILURE AND NO ASSISTANCE WAS PROVIDED.
THE CONTACT WAS UNSURE IF THE RENTAL COMPANY NOTIFIED THE DEALER AND MANUFACTURER.

questions.note: Only 11205702. 11204698 does not count: the contact was unsure whether the rental company notified the manufacturer (merely possible). 11229137 reported to the dealership and 11209676 names only the dealer.

questions.question: Did the owner in complaint 11176393 have an issue like this with their earlier Outbacks?

expected.text: No. They had multiple Outbacks in the past and never had an issue like this.

chunks.quote: HAD MULTIPLE OUTBACKS IN THE PAST AND NEVER HAD AN ISSUE LIKE THIS.

questions.question: What failure mileage does complaint 11204698 report?

chunks.quote: THE FAILURE MILEAGE WAS 5,218.

questions.question: What is Honda's own number for recall 16V725000?

chunks.quote: Honda's number for this recall is KC6.

questions.question: What will dealers do under recall 26V011000?

expected.text: Replace the engine block heater, free of charge.

chunks.quote: Dealers will replace the block heater, free of charge.

questions.note: The alternative of a threaded plug in place of the heater element is an option offered to owners, not the dealers' remedy; an answer may mention it.

questions.question: On what date did recall 19V576000 begin?

chunks.quote: The recall began September 27, 2019.

questions.question: How many miles does the owner in complaint 11166434 say are on their 2019 Outback?

chunks.quote: I HAVE 3200 MILES ON MY 2019 OUTBACK

questions.question: Which dealership did the owner in complaint 11205702 take the vehicle to?

expected.text: Toyota of North Scranton, 3400 N Main Ave, Scranton, PA.

chunks.quote: THE VEHICLE WAS TAKEN TO TOYOTA OF NORTH SCRANTON (3400 N MAIN AVE, SCRANTON, PA 18508, (570) 489-7584)

questions.note: Naming Toyota of North Scranton is enough; the address is optional.

questions.question: What is the NHTSA action number of recall campaign 25V695000?
questions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT unnest(results, recursive := true) FROM recalls) SELECT NHTSAActionNumber FROM r WHERE NHTSACampaignNumber = '25V695000'

questions.question: For how many days was the vehicle in complaint 10692693 in the Ford repair shop?

chunks.quote: VEHICLE WAS IN FORD REPAIR SHOP FOR 12 DAYS
